code_written_limitations: Unallocated complaints (computed by code from `area_rollup.json`): 22.8% (A19) of complaint and cancellation records (56 (A10)) are general/unspecified: generic criticism (for example "worst update") that names no specific area, so they are not allocated to any of the four decision areas. If many of them refer to one area's problem, for example the same free-tier change, that area's total is understated; the labels cannot show which area that would be.

Premium-only boundary, upper-bound sensitivity (computed by code; `analysis/premium_only_sensitivity.json`): 7 (T57) of the 45 (C01) `billing.premium_only` complaint and cancellation records contain no Premium or payment word (premium, subscri-, pay/paid/paying, free, buy, money, trial, $; case-insensitive), with a severity sum of 21 (T58). If none of them belonged to billing/support, its severity sum would fall from 158 (A05) to 137 (T59), below playback/performance 159 (A02) and usability 140 (A08). This is an upper bound, not a relabelling: many of these reviews plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle), and they were not moved to any other area.
mandatory_limitations: Counts describe the labeled reviews in a 500-review development checkpoint (checkpoint_500.csv), not the full corpus: self-selected public app reviews, not a customer population. They carry no revenue, plan tier or confirmed cancellations, so revenue at risk cannot be computed.
Cancellation language is expressed intent, not observed churn; nothing here estimates a causal effect on retention.
Star ratings and helpful votes were not used to classify; severity is judged from the text under the shared rubric.
31 completed records are flagged needs_review, 0 are quarantined and 0 are unfinished.

alternatives.why_not_first: Billing/support's baseline severity sum {A05} is close to but below playback/performance's {A02}, and its complaint share {T22} is higher than playback/performance's {T25} (intervals overlap). Its leading issue, premium-only restrictions (severity sum {C02} across {C01} reviews), is a free-tier packaging and entitlement policy matter, not a playback defect, and a spike-month increase of {T40} in {T37} inflates its recent visibility without changing the full-window severity-sum ordering.

Usability has the highest complaint count and share of complaints ({T19}, overlapping with billing/support and playback/performance), and leads the verifier's sampled severity-sum ordering under both labelers, but its full-sample baseline severity sum {A08} is below playback/performance's {A02}, and its share-of-reviews growth between {T01} and {T02} ({T18}) is smaller than playback/performance's ({T15}).

Access/onboarding has by far the lowest baseline severity sum {A17} and the lowest share of complaints {T28} (its interval does not overlap with any other area), and its share-of-reviews change between {T01} and {T02} ({T09}) is the smallest among the four decision areas.

limitations: The verifier's labelling disagreement (top area usability rather than playback/performance on the same severity-sum metric) is based on a small sampled subset ({T43} reviews) and cannot by itself confirm which ordering holds in the full set of {S07} ranked complaint and cancellation reviews.

Complaint-share sampling intervals for usability, billing/support, and playback/performance all overlap each other, so the full-sample complaint-share ordering among these three areas cannot be treated as firmly distinguished.
The period comparison between {T01} and {T02} reflects self-selected reviewers in each window and differing total review volumes ({T03} versus {T05}), not a measured customer population change.
Severity labels reflect the enrichment process's judgment of review text, not independently verified support-ticket or crash-telemetry severity.
next_quarter_actions: Investigate and reduce playback stopping or skipping mid-track (issue playback.stops, severity sum {C14} across {C13} reviews), targeting a reduction in this issue's complaint count and severity sum next quarter.
Triage and fix post-update app crashes and blank-screen loads (issue playback.crash, severity sum {C26} across {C25} reviews), aiming to lower this issue's complaint count.
Diagnose the false offline/no-internet error (issue playback.connection, severity sum {C30} across {C29} reviews) to reduce its share of complaints.

As a hedge on the strongest alternative area, review the premium-only restrictions issue (billing.premium_only, severity sum {C02} across {C01} reviews) as a free-tier packaging and entitlement policy question, watching whether its share of complaints or trend share changes.
rationale: Baseline priority (severity sum over complaint and cancellation reviews) is highest for playback/performance at {A02}, ahead of billing/support at {A05}, usability at {A08}, and access/onboarding at {A17}.

Playback/performance also shows the largest increase among the four decision areas in share of reviews between {T01} and {T02}, rising from {T13} to {T14}, a change of {T15}, larger than billing/support's {T12}, usability's {T18}, or access/onboarding's {T09}.

On share of complaints, usability's {T19} is higher than playback/performance's {T25}, and billing/support's {T22} also sits above playback/performance's share point estimate, though all three intervals overlap each other (playback/performance's interval does not overlap with access/onboarding's), so playback/performance leads on severity sum but not on complaint count or share of complaints.

A caveat for robustness: in the verifier's sampled relabeling ({T43} reviews), usability is the top area under both enricher and verifier labels on the same row-weighted severity-sum metric, while playback/performance ranks second under enricher labels and third under verifier labels; this is a labelling disagreement with the full-sample baseline ordering and makes the recommendation provisional.

A spike month {T37} shows the largest increase for billing's premium-only issue ({T40}), not for a playback/performance issue, so the playback/performance recommendation does not rest on spike-month evidence.
output.recommendation: We recommend directing next quarter's product-improvement effort to playback/performance, which carries the highest baseline priority among the four decision areas, driven by playback stopping or skipping (severity sum {C14} across {C13} complaint and cancellation reviews), app crashes after update (severity sum {C26} across {C25} reviews), false offline or no-internet errors (severity sum {C30} across {C29} reviews), and downloads disappearing or failing (severity sum {C34} across {C33} reviews). This is core playback reliability and stability engineering work, not a packaging or entitlement question.
what_would_change_the_call: A larger verified sample confirming the verifier's severity-sum ordering (usability above playback/performance, as seen in {T47} versus {T49}) would weaken the case for playback/performance over usability.

A human audit of the {T57} premium-only records without a Premium or payment word finding that most genuinely describe free-tier restrictions would support billing/support's severity sum staying near {A05} rather than falling toward {T59}, narrowing the gap with playback/performance.

If playback/performance's share of reviews reverses back toward {T13} in the same months of the following year rather than holding near {T14}, the growth basis for this recommendation would no longer apply.

payload.question: Where should the next quarter of product-improvement effort go: access/onboarding, usability, playback/performance, or billing/support?

top_issues.definition: Features locked to Premium: skip limits, forced shuffle, cannot pick songs, cannot repeat or rewind, lyrics or offline behind a paywall, 'everything needs Premium now'.
top_issues.name: Premium-only restrictions
top_issues.summary: Free users are frustrated that core playback controls like skipping, song selection, repeat, and shuffle toggling are locked behind a Premium subscription.

top_issues.definition: General praise or criticism with no specific feature, unrelated content (politics, artists, boycotts), or meaningless text.
top_issues.name: General or unrelated

top_issues.definition: Too many, too long, too loud or repeated ads; ads interrupting listening.
top_issues.name: Excessive Ad Interruptions
top_issues.summary: Customers report that frequent, lengthy, and repeated ads interrupt music playback, making the free listening experience frustrating and disruptive.

top_issues.definition: Music stops, pauses, skips by itself, will not start, or plays the wrong song.
top_issues.name: Playback stops or skips
top_issues.summary: Users report that songs fail to play, randomly stop or skip mid-track, or play the wrong song, disrupting their listening experience.

top_issues.definition: Hard to find things, confusing layout, redesigns or home-screen changes, buttons moved or removed.
top_issues.name: Confusing redesigned home screen layout
top_issues.summary: Customers report that recent redesigns and home-screen changes made it harder to locate playlists, daily mixes, and other features they previously accessed easily.

top_issues.definition: Cannot log in, keeps getting logged out, login or verification-code errors.
top_issues.name: Login failures
top_issues.summary: Users are unexpectedly logged out of their accounts and then cannot log back in due to password, verification, token, or connectivity errors.

top_issues.definition: App crashes, freezes, will not open or load, blank screens.
top_issues.name: App crashes and fails to load after update
top_issues.summary: Customers report the app crashes, freezes, or gets stuck on a blank or loading screen, often after updating, preventing normal use.

top_issues.definition: App says there is no internet or that it is offline while connected; network or streaming errors.
top_issues.name: False offline/no-internet error
top_issues.summary: The app incorrectly reports no internet connection despite an active connection, blocking playback and content loading.

top_issues.definition: Downloading, saved music, offline mode, downloads that disappear or fail.
top_issues.name: Downloads disappear or fail to work
top_issues.summary: Customers report that downloaded songs vanish, offline mode fails to play without internet, and downloads get stuck.

top_issues.definition: Managing the queue, playlists, liked songs or library; shuffle or repeat controls that misbehave.
top_issues.name: Shuffle and playlist controls malfunctioning
top_issues.summary: Customers report shuffle repeating songs or playing randomly against preference, and difficulty accessing or viewing their playlists and liked songs.

period_comparison.comparison_scope: areas lists the four decision areas only; areas that are not decision options are under non_decision_areas
period_comparison.method: share = complaint/cancellation reviews in the area / all classified reviews in the period; Wilson 95% intervals; identical calendar months one year apart avoid the partial first/last months and seasonal mix. Descriptive only: reviews are self-selected, not a customer census.

premium_only_sensitivity.interpretation: Upper-bound sensitivity, not a relabelling. It assumes that none of the records without a Premium or payment word belongs in billing/support and adds them to no other area. Many of them plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle, no repeat or rewind), and non-English payment words (for example 'paisa') are not matched, so the real effect is smaller than shown.
premium_only_sensitivity.what: upper-bound sensitivity of the billing/support lead to the premium-only topic boundary, computed by code; not a relabelling

spike_months.measure: the issue's complaint and cancellation reviews as a share of all reviews in the month, minus the same share in the other full months (share of reviews)
the issue's complaint and cancellation reviews as a share of all reviews in the month, minus the same share in the other full months (share of reviews)

verifier_robustness.metric: severity_sum (the baseline priority) over complaint and cancellation reviews, row-weighted

top_by_complaint_count.note: area names only, no counts: state in words, cite no token

unallocated_complaints.what: complaint and cancellation records labelled with no specific area (generic criticism); not allocated to any decision area
